characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy coordinates the project’s demonstrator work, selecting approaches, architectures, and evaluation criteria to prove platform-neutral or fallback authentication concepts. It defines scope, risk budgets, and success metrics (e.g., credible evidence from non-production demonstrators, resilience of fallback paths, and interoperability with open standards such as FIDO2 and OpenID Connect). It guides resource allocation, screens trade-offs between methods, and provides a defensible technical baseline for policy and procurement discussions. Success is measured by demonstrator integrity, documented technical risks, and a credible roadmap for phase two demonstrations.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever creates credibility for the coalition by delivering credible demonstrations that inform policy, while supplying concrete inputs for procurement language. It has strong synergy with Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) and Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551) by translating tech results into persuasive, action-ready materials.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Technical Feasibility Strategy may constrain budget and timelines, potentially limiting breadth of demonstrators. Focusing on a narrow method can clash with Policy Advocacy Strategy's broad coalition goals and EU Standards Engagement Strategy's desire for diverse, standards-aligned demonstrations. These tensions require trade-offs between depth and breadth.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the policy narrative and procurement requirements to advance platform-neutral access. It translates resilience and continuity concerns into concrete policy proposals, stakeholder engagement plans, and regulatory arguments. It coordinates with coalition and procurement levers to pull through language in digital-identity procurement documents, standards calls, and AltID-related processes. Success metrics include formal proposals submitted, coalition endorsements, and early statements from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. The strategy also anticipates political resistance and reserves channels for privacy and democratic accountability dialogue. It remains sensitive to vendor influence, regulatory delay, and public scrutiny.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy benefits from Coalition Building Strategy’s broad support and EU Standards Engagement Strategy’s interoperability framing. By weaving resilience rhetoric into policy proposals, it accelerates adoption of platform-neutral standards (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) and aligns with EU-level discussions (2e9016aa-8563-447e-a5e0-0e146f4ebad3). It also sustains momentum for procurement and oversight channels.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy Advocacy Strategy may encounter regulatory capture risk if too alliance-focused, weakening privacy or democratic accountability messaging. It can conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if messaging is too narrow or adversarial, fragmenting support. It must balance continuity with privacy concerns and EU alignment that may slow progress.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy focuses on growing a broad, diverse supporter base to bolster policy momentum. It identifies and engages civil-society groups, privacy advocates, researchers, security practitioners, and public-policy stakeholders, aligning their messaging around resilience, procurement neutrality, and continuity. It emphasizes transparent governance, risk sharing, and coordinated outreach to Folketinget committees and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. Success is measured by coalition size, alignment on core objectives, and joint deliverables such as letters or public briefings. Risks include internal trade-offs and conflicting priorities requiring clear governance and decision rights.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Coalition Building Strategy gains momentum when Policy Advocacy Strategy provides concrete proposals and EU Standards Engagement Strategy anchors cross-border legitimacy. This synergy reduces messaging fragmentation and aligns civil-society voices with EU interoperability goals, strengthening advocacy across government, regulators, and researchers.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Coalition Building Strategy may struggle with internal governance; conflicts between stakeholders can slow progress and risk dilution of core platform-neutral aims. It could clash with Procurement Influence Strategy if coalition pushes broad demands that procurement cannot satisfy or if privacy advocates resist compromise.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy seeks to embed platform-neutral language and certified fallback requirements into AltID procurement documents and related contracts. It translates demonstrator results, policy proposals, and EU standards signals into concrete procurement criteria, supplier-diversity incentives, and evaluation metrics. The strategy aims to accelerate adoption of platform-neutral models and reduce long-term dependency on Apple and Google by shaping procurement incentives rather than relying on regulation alone. Success is demonstrated by updated procurement language, measurable supplier diversity, and sign-off from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen or other authorities.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Procurement Influence Strategy gains power when Technical Feasibility Strategy translates demonstrator outcomes into concrete procurement criteria, and when Coalition Building Strategy broadens stakeholder buy-in for those criteria. This alignment helps ensure that vendor responses address real technical risks and procurement realities.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement Influence Strategy risks gaming procurement or creating perverse incentives if language is too generic. It may conflict with Technical Feasibility Strategy if demonstrated capabilities outpace procurement readiness, or with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if national procurement diverges from EU-aligned criteria.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy coordinates active participation in EU bodies and technical working groups to influence interoperability, portability, and anti-lock-in requirements. It captures input into eIDAS2, NSIS, and the European Digital Identity Wallet framework, aligning national policy with Europe-wide objectives. The strategy seeks to create pull for platform-neutral architectures by forecasting standards, publishing position papers, and securing early commitments from EU actors. Success is measured by formal EU inputs, alignment of national initiatives with DW discussions, and adoption of platform-neutral language in EU Digital Identity Wallet materials.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy gains impact when Technical Feasibility Strategy proves standards-aligned demonstrators, and when Policy Advocacy Strategy leverages EU alignment to push national procurement and policy. It also strengthens Coalition Building Strategy by providing Europe-wide legitimacy for platform-neutral aims. IDs: (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), (80b177d0-c67e-4bc2-bd50-3f49b815e633).
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU Standards Engagement Strategy could face conflict with national procurement timelines and sovereignty concerns if EU-standard progress is slow or contested. It may marginalize rapid national pilots favored by the Policy Advocacy or Coalition Building levers, risking misalignment with AltID procurement milestones.
